$description: AntFabric UI design tokens in the W3C Design Tokens Format Module 2025.10. Generated by `pnpm tokens:build` from packages/core/src/tokens.ts (values), packages/core/src/descriptions.ts (descriptions) and packages/core/tokens.map.json (sources): do not edit it, change those and run the command again; `pnpm check` fails when this file is stale. A token's $value is its light-theme (colours, shadows) or desktop-profile (sizes, type, density) value; a token that is the same everywhere has only that. A token that varies by mode lists every mode's value in $extensions["com.antfabric"].modes: { light, dark } or { web, desktop, mobile }, with an OS key (android) where that OS changes the value of the profile it extends (modes.os at the root says which). A token only some profiles have lists them in onlyIn. Dimensions are px; the phone reads px as pt. Where the format cannot say a value exactly (a percentage, em, a gradient angle, no shadow), $value is the closest it can say and $extensions["com.antfabric"].css keeps the string the kits use. A $value in braces, "{primitives.color.neutral.900}", points at a primitive of the product's Tier 1 in the `primitives` group at the end of this file, which holds the primitives some token points at (the whole mirror is packages/core/src/primitives.ts); a token that has drifted from the product, has no product token or has no primitive of its own holds its value. A $value that names another token, "{border.subtle}", is an alias: the token is that one, in every mode, and follows it when a theme changes it. Each token's $extensions["com.antfabric"] says its tier (semantic: a role any component reads; component: owned by the components listed in `component`) and `visibility: internal` where it is left out of the documented set.

page.$description: Ground the panes sit on: near-white ash in light, with white cards held off it by an outline. Read by no component yet.

card.$description: The default card, pane and field surface: things that sit on the page. Things that float above it use raised.

com.antfabric.sourceNote: the product calls the default pane/card surface `card`

raised.$description: Menus, popovers, toasts and hover cards: surfaces that float above content. White in light, a step lighter than default in dark so the lift shows.

chrome.$description: Nav rail, title bar and breadcrumb strip: the surfaces you navigate from. Equals default in light today, but stays separate so chrome can retint alone.

sidebar.$description: The channels sidebar alone, a shade off white so a list you scan reads apart from the rail. Avatar stacks on it ring in this.

recessed.$description: A strip set slightly back inside a card: table headers, sub-toolbars, empty-state insets, the syncing banner. Lighter than the page in light.

muted.$description: Grey fill for disabled fields, progress tracks, empty-state tiles and badges. Matches selected in light; use selected for the current row.

selected.$description: The current row in a navigation list: open channel, folder or item. One step stronger than hover, and the two never stack.

unread.$description: Faint coral tint on an unread message or notification row: 3 per cent in light, 5 in dark. A hint, not a highlight.

inverse.$description: Dark ink fill for tooltips, toasts and the dark button. Flips to near-white in dark so it still contrasts with the page.

inverseHover.$description: Wash behind a control on color.background.inverse when it is hovered, such as the remove cross of an active filter chip. Light on the dark ink in light, dark on the near-white in dark, so it shows in both.

com.antfabric.sourceNote: ours: the hover wash on a control drawn on surface.inverse (an active filter chip's remove cross); the product has no inverse washes. Light is white at 16%; dark is the page ink (--charcoal-950-alpha-16), since inverse turns near-white there

inverseWash.$description: Resting fill of a small element laid on color.background.inverse, such as an inverse key cap. Light on the dark ink in light, dark on the near-white in dark, so it shows in both.
